title: A simple microplastic splitter for subsampling expanded polystyrene particles
author: Nakajima, Isobe, et al.

steps.title: Prepare particle batch
steps.instruction: Select the polymer type (virgin EPS, environmental EPS, virgin PE, or virgin PP) and obtain exactly 80 particles (mean diameters: virgin EPS 1.5 ± 0.15 mm, environmental EPS 2.6 ± 0.58 mm, PE 3.4 ± 0.20 mm, PP 4.1 ± 0.09 mm; n = 20 for each size measurement).

steps.title: Place particles in seawater
steps.instruction: Transfer the 80 particles into a clean glass dish containing seawater and stir the suspension thoroughly to achieve a uniform distribution.

steps.title: Insert radial splitter
steps.instruction: Position the radial microplastic splitter centrally in the glass dish so that the dish is divided into eight equal compartments labeled A through H.

steps.title: Count particles per compartment
steps.instruction: After the splitter is in place, count the number of particles present in each of the eight compartments (A–H) and record the counts.

steps.title: Repeat measurements
steps.instruction: Remove the splitter, remix the sample, and repeat steps 2–4 a total of ten independent replicates, recording counts for each replicate.

steps.title: Calculate subsampling error
steps.instruction: For each compartment, compute the subsampling error using: Subsampling error = (number of particles in the compartment × 8) / 80.

steps.title: Compute statistics
steps.instruction: For each compartment and for the overall dataset, calculate the mean, standard deviation (SD), and coefficient of variation (CV = SD / mean × 100%).

steps.title: Perform statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Test normality with a chi‑square test and homogeneity of variance with a Bartlett test. Then conduct a one‑way ANOVA on the compartment counts; consider differences significant at p < 0.05.
